question.name: The Weather Dance That Went Wrong
question.text: A confident performer claims to have perfected a new weather dance.

choices.label: Ask for a demonstration without grand promises.

a1.text: Rain arrives, but only after the dancer has exhausted every spectator. The farmers celebrate.

text_only.reason: only the farmers celebrate, and they are not cast; told only

a2.text: A gust of wind carries away ceremonial decorations. The audience applauds, thinking it part of the performance.

a3.text: No rain falls. The dancer insists that the clouds are simply late.

a4.text: A brief shower falls on the wrong patch of ground. The researchers argue whether it counts.

b1.text: The dancer admits the ritual was mostly improvisation and learns humility.

b2.text: An elder turns the performance into a children's game.

b3.text: Careful observations of wind and clouds lead to a useful prediction.
